attacks.unsupported_mechanism: KILLED - The record claims a 4-log kill in a 0.1-0.3 s sea-chest grating transit at up to 80 NTU turbidity using a 12 kW pulsed UV-C LED ring, but UV-C fluence required for 4-log inactivation of representative entrained organisms (e.g., bacteria, phytoplankton, zooplankton larvae) is on the order of 10-100 mJ/cm²; even at 12 kW delivered to a grating cross-section with a typical UV-C LED wall-plug efficiency of a few percent and at 80 NTU where UV transmittance collapses (UVT typically <50% and often <20% at 80 NTU for 254 nm-equivalent paths), the achievable in-water fluence in a 0.1-0.3 s sub-second transit is orders of magnitude below what the 4-log claim requires — a defect derivable from the record's own 0.2 s transit, 12 kW supply, and 80 NTU turbidity boundary.
